content.passage: Alice Guy-Blaché directed hundreds of films between 1896 and 1920. She wanted audiences to feel like they were watching real people on screen. Guy-Blaché often encourages actors in her films to behave naturally, giving rise to a directing style named "le Naturaliste." At the same time, many of Guy-Blaché's films, at times, lacked sound, so actors had to rely solely on their bodies and facial expressions. To achieve this, she sometimes instructed her actors to highly exaggerate their actions and expressions. The style of acting in Guy-Blaché's films was _______.
content.question_text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: very modern by Guy-Blaché's peers.
choices.B: familiar to actors who had worked on other directors’ films.
choices.C: very unusual for the period.
choices.D: better than film acting today.

content.explanation: Choice C is the best answer. The text explains that actors tended to highly exaggerate their actions and expressions in films produced from 1896 to 1920. This suggests that this was an uncommon style during Guy-Blaché's time, hence 'very unusual for the period.'

content.passage: In these poems in her 2017 collection One Last Word, poet Nikki Grimes used a writing method called the golden shovel. This involves choosing a line from an existing poem and then using each word from that line as the last word of each line in a new poem. Grimes wanted the poems in One Last Word to honor important Black poets of the past, so she chose lines by poets such as Langston Hughes and Georgia Douglas Johnson. Writing in this way can be challenging and might seem as though it would produce awkward poems. However, reviewers praised her One Last Word poems.
content.question_text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: Most reviewers didn't understand Grimes’s goal to honor these poets.
choices.B: Creating new forms of poetry can be very difficult.
choices.C: Langston Hughes and Georgia Douglas Johnson are two of the most well-known Black poets.
choices.D: Critics thought her poems reflected Grimes’s goal of honoring the poets she admires.

content.explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it most logically completes the text's discussion of Nikki Grimes's poetry collection One Last Word: that reviewers appreciated the poems and recognized Grimes's intention to honor the poets of the past.

content.passage: Researchers wanted to study how consumers’ reactions to an ad were affected by the number of ads. The researchers began by showing study participants either no ads, seeing an ad once, or seeing a less detailed ad and others seeing a more detailed ad. Participants who had seen the more detailed ad rated the product more highly. The researchers found that reactions to an ad may be affected by _______ in ways that people don’t expect.
content.question_text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: the number of people who viewed the ad.
choices.B: the length of time viewing previous ads.
choices.C: the assessment of ad detail by the researchers.
choices.D: the time of day that the ad is aired.

content.explanation: Choice C is the best answer. The passage tells us that participants who had seen a less detailed ad for a product beforehand rated the more detailed version higher, which implies that the perception of an ad is affected by the detail of previous ads.

content.passage: The musical Hadestown was produced off-Broadway in New York in 2016. A revised version of the musical premiered on Broadway in 2019, in a larger production. choices.A: The 2016 version of Hadestown had fewer storytelling problems than the 2019 version did.
choices.B: Hadestown should be rewritten to address plot issues.
choices.C: The 2019 version is an improved version of the musical.
choices.D: Hadestown greatly improved between 2016 and its premiere on Broadway.

content.explanation: Choice A is the best answer because it most logically completes the text's discussion of critic Jesse Green's review of the 2016 and 2019 productions of Hadestown, indicating that the earlier version had fewer plot problems.

content.passage: In her 2021 article 'Throwaway History: Towards a Historiography of Ephemera,' scholar Anne Garner discusses John Johnson (1882–1956), a devoted collector of items intended to be discarded, including bus tickets and campaign pamphlets. Johnson recognized that scholarly institutions considered his expansive collection of ephemeral items to be worthless, indeed it wasn’t until 1968, after Johnson’s death, that Oxford University’s Bodleian Library acquired the collection, having grasped the items’ potential value to historians and other researchers. Here, the example of Johnson serves to -
content.question_text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: demonstrate the difficulties faced by contemporary historians in conducting research at the Bodleian Library without access to ephemera.
choices.B: explain the challenge of incorporating examples of ephemera into the collections of libraries and other scholarly institutions.
choices.C: lend support to arguments by historians and other researchers that collections of ephemeral material may offer insights not possible by other means.
choices.D: illustrate both the relatively slow manner in which scholarly institutions come to recognize the potential importance of new scholarly output.

content.explanation: Choice C is the best answer because it most logically completes the text’s discussion of the potential importance of ephemeral items for historians.

content.passage: The practice of logging (cutting down trees for commercial use) is often thought to be at odds with forest conservation (the work of preserving forests). However, a massive study in forest preservation and expansion spanning 700,000 hectares in Oregon’s Malheur National Forest calls that view into question. For instance, the study revealed that forest plots that have undergone limited logging (the careful removal of a controlled number of trees) may be more robust than plots that haven’t been logged at all. These results, in turn, suggest that -
content.question_text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: logging may be useful for maintaining healthy forests, provided it is limited.
choices.B: other practices besides logging serve to positively impact forest health.
choices.C: as time passes, it will be difficult to know whether forest health was improved by logging.
choices.D: unlogged forests are generally considered less healthy than logged forests.

content.explanation: Choice A is the best answer because it logically completes the text’s discussion of the potential effects of logging on forest health that the study presents by stating that logging, when undertaken in a limited way, may benefit forests.

choices.A: the interpersonal benefits of some interruptions in the workplace may offset the productivity losses they cause.
choices.B: in order to maximize productivity, employers should be willing to interpret employee interruptions differently throughout the day.
choices.C: most employees avoid interrupting colleagues because they don’t appreciate being interrupted themselves.
choices.D: in order to cultivate an ideal workplace environment, employers should mandate breaks whenever possible.

content.explanation: Choice A is the best answer because it most logically completes the text’s discussion of potential benefits of interruptions in the workplace.

content.passage: Songbirds learn to imitate and refine their species’ songs from an early age. With each generation, small differences are introduced that result in distinct dialects—vocalizations among geographically isolated populations of the same species. A research study examined whether two-day-old Filolatu hypoleuca (pied flycatcher) nestlings prefer local dialects over the unfamiliar dialects of conspecifics: F hypoleuca populations—the more closely the nestlings made in response to a song, the stronger their preference. choices.B: the preference of F. hypoleuca nestlings for their own dialect may indicate that chicks have an incentive to modify the nestlings they raise in order to produce more song in the species.
choices.C: notation using International Phonetic Alphabet allows scientists to determine whether F. hypoleuca dialects exhibited socialization between geographically isolated populations.
choices.D: birds from the same region feel more attracted by the local dialect of F. hypoleuca, and as such only prefer the local dialects over those formed by other species.

However, there is no evidence of significant spikes in carbon dioxide levels coinciding with relevant periods in sauropod evolution, such as when the first large sauropods appeared, when several sauropod lineages underwent further evolution toward gigantism, or when sauropods reached their maximum known sizes, suggesting that ___________
content.question_text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: fluctuations in atmospheric carbon dioxide levels could not have directly increased sauropod size.
choices.B: another factor like volcanic activity spurred sauropod evolution.
choices.C: sauropods would have increased in size regardless of the conditions.
choices.D: vegetation alone caused the giant sizes of sauropods.

content.explanation: Choice A is the most plausible conclusion based on the given information about carbon dioxide levels and sauropod evolution.

content.passage: The Cretaceous pterosaur Tupandactylus navigans is known for having an anomalously oversized head crest. Until a more complete fossil skeleton was found in Brazil, paleontologists had been able to study only skull specimens from T. navigans, though it was presumed that, like other pterosaurs, the species' primary form of locomotion was powered flight. Examining the fuller skeleton in 2016, Victor Beccari and his team determined that T. navigans had long hind legs, short wings, and an unusually long neck—characteristics that, combined with the massive head crest, meant the species would have had sustained flight difficult and walking upright relatively comfortable. Based on these findings the team suggested that ___________
content.question_text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: T. navigans would only require short flights, implying that it could have walked longer distances.
choices.B: the distance that other pterosaur species considered the norm is quite small.
choices.C: it would spend more time on walking than its relatives.
choices.D: the species did not evolve as a result of later developed species flight abilities.

content.explanation: Choice C makes logical sense as the characteristics described imply the species was more adapted for walking than sustained flight.

However, a group of researchers recently viewed a ‘major component of the Dutch diet’ argument with skepticism because only a handful of painters depicted those foods with any frequency, and even they needed them for warmer climates—features in Dutch paintings of the period that more often do not truly show realistic conditions, thereby casting doubt on the dairy products’ importance.
content.question_text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: dairy products were a more significant component of the Dutch diet of the period than lemons were.
choices.B: food was more popular subject matter for Dutch painters whose art was aiming towards better commerce sharing.
choices.C: depictions of food in Dutch painting should focus on making realistic representations of those existing habits.
choices.D: the public demand of the period had depicted more foods for symbolic reasons rather than to show what Dutch eating habits were.

content.explanation: Choice D makes logical sense considering the discussion on symbolic representation rather than realism within art.

content.passage: To investigate the nature of plate subduction—when one of Earth’s tectonic plates slips beneath another—Sarah M. Aarons and colleagues compared ancient rocks from the Acasta Gneiss Complex in Canada to modern rocks. Using isotope analysis, the researchers found that Acasta rocks dating to about 4.02 billion years ago (bya) most strongly resemble modern rocks formed in a plume setting (an area in which hot materials rise from below Earth’s outer layer to the crust). By contrast, they found that Acasta rocks formed later (at about 3.75 bya) have more in common with rocks formed by modern subduction. On this basis, Aarons and her colleagues proposed that by about 3.75 bya, subduction and related rock-forming processes had begun, meaning Acasta rocks provide evidence that some of Earth’s earliest tectonic shifts had occurred by that time.
content.question_text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: subduction processes began occurring in some locations no later than 3.75 bya.
choices.B: the subduction process forms modern rocks that resemble those formed billions of years ago.
choices.C: the oldest rocks in the Acasta Gneiss Complex formed through subduction.
choices.D: subduction replaced mantle plume formation as the most common geological process about 3.5 billion years ago.

content.explanation: Choice A is the best answer because it logically complements the text’s discussion of Aarons and her colleagues’ investigation, indicating the geological processes that must have been occurring for the formation of the observed rock types. Nothing in the passage suggests that these dates are wrong.

content.passage: In 2016 biological anthropologist Heather J. Smith and her team investigated the evolution of the appendix, an intestinal organ that is present in some mammals, including humans, but is generally thought to have no function. Studying 533 mammal species, the team found that the appendix is more likely to appear in mammals that possess cecums, a structure associated with immune response, and that the appendix itself has independently, and repeatedly, evolved more than 30 times. Notably, species with the organ tend to have higher concentrations of lymphoid tissue—which supports immune responses. Therefore, the team hypothesized that the appendix may
content.question_text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: increase an individual’s chances of survival.
choices.B: have evolved in species that do not possess cecums.
choices.C: will emerge in a greater number of mammal species as it performs a necessary function in the immune system.
choices.D: produced higher concentrations of lymphoid tissue in some organs.

content.explanation: Choice C is the best answer because it most logically complements the text’s discussion of Smith and colleagues’ investigation into the evolution and presence of the appendix by linking the presence of this organ to immune system functionality.

content.passage: Zines are small-scale, self-published magazines. They have been around since the Black literary zine *Fire!!* was created in the 1920s. Since then, zines have appealed to creators looking for a relatively easy and inexpensive way to share a self-selected audience. Zine creators often mix art with social commentary and challenge mainstream ideas. At first, the internet appeared to replace the zine, but this has not been the case. There are enough zines in the United States to support an annual zine festival. This suggests that ______.
content.question_text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: creators can reach a larger audience by posting online.
choices.B: zines are still a meaningful form of expression.
choices.C: zine creators continue to explore new art forms.
choices.D: most zines are successful commercially.

content.explanation: Choice B is the best answer because it presents the conclusion most logically from the text’s point about zines today. The text describes zines as small-scale, self-published magazines that appeal to creators looking to reach selective audiences inexpensively (lines 2-5). Zines gain an audience by challenging mainstream ideas and not targeting financial success (choice A), so it is unlikely being online would greatly increase their audience as other forms do. While zines do appeal to some creators, it does not fully suggest creators 'explore different art forms' (C); many remain traditional self-publishing mediums to exchange specific views. Likewise, most statements explicitly explain the creators' intentions as small rather than commercial success (D). Thus, every sentence indicates that zines persist rather than view succeeding commercially, rather suggesting choice B. The use of the plural form — zines continue to be in demand and appeal — implies the overall relevance of zines.

content.passage: Astronomers investigating the Arabia Terra region of Mars believe that it appears to contain irregularly shaped craters that may have been caused by massive volcanic explosions. In their investigations of Arabia Terra, the researchers found remnants of ash deposits in amounts and thickness that would have resulted from a massive volcanic eruption. However, erosion and past resurfacing events could have modified the surface of the planet. Therefore, ______.
content.question_text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: current knowledge of the Arabia Terra region might not accurately reflect the volcanic activity of Mars's past.
choices.B: eruptions from Mars’s volcanoes were likely more disastrous than other volcanic eruptions.
choices.C: Arabia Terra holds evidence for multiple different volcanoes on Mars’s surface.
choices.D: Mars was most likely expelled from multiple explosions as far as thousands of kilometers away.

content.explanation: Choice A is the best answer because it presents the conclusion most logically follows from the text’s discussions of the Arabia Terra region and volcanic craters. The passage discusses findings in Arabia Terra that the patterns appear to have been influenced by massive volcanic eruptions, supported by remnants of ash deposits that would result from a volcanic eruption due to richness and intensification. This effect, along with planetary resurfacing, poses some potential modification to the terrain (e.g., erosion), contributing to limitations on current assessments. As a result, the only conclusion that can reasonably be drawn involving these changes remains that present knowledge concerning Arabia Terra might ultimately be imprecise about Mars’s past volcanic activity. None of the remaining choices (B, C, D) focus on descriptions of Mars’s volcanic or explosive events; nor do they concentrate relevant detail exclusively involving planetary erosion or about the landscape, offering declines surrounding conceptions within the text itself.

content.passage: The ancient Sumerian civilization formed around 4000 BCE between two large rivers in an area that is now Iraq and Syria. The extremely hot and sunny weather in that area helped crops grow very quickly, but it also made it hard to keep the crops from drying up and dying. So, the Sumerians used water from the rivers in their farming. However, they even had to augment their system by creating ______.
content.question_text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: harvested crops only on the hottest days of summer.
choices.B: allowed crops to dry during the hottest days of summer.
choices.C: harvested crops only after 4000 BCE.
choices.D: harvested as much as they could during the dry season.

content.explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it presents the conclusion most logically completes the text's understanding of the Sumerian civilization and climate in the regions affecting farming. They provide descriptions of both favorable sunshine and heat but highlight struggles against drought that threaten cultivated crops (lines 2-4). Consequentially, irrigation was employed widely sustaining crops and teaching adaptations that encourage adjustments to water resource management ultimately suggests that harvesting would align with choice D. Choices A and C suggest an impractical, inefficient strategy only supported by extreme conditions not elaborated by the text’s exploration. Choice B lacks evidentiary reinforcement and contradicts the adaptive urgency portrayed, further distancing itself from implicit organizational actions surrounding food priorities.

content.passage: Red velvet cake has been a favorite dessert of many for years, but the recipe’s origins are unclear. A bakery in Dallas, Texas, argued that it created the first recipe for red velvet cake when their bakery opened in the 1860s. The Adams Extract Co., which sells baking products, claims to have created the recipe in the 1930s to help market their red dye. A US hotel and a Canadian department store also publicly stated that red velvet cake sold in each of their establishments in the 1930s was an original creation, each alleging that it was the recipe author. No clear evidence has emerged to favor one of these claims over the others. ______
content.question_text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: A red velvet cake was not actually developed in the 1860s.
choices.B: Three American locations began selling red velvet cake by the 1930s.
choices.C: The cake likely originated from a family recipe.

For instance, Romeo and Juliet, which is set in the Italy of Shakespeare’s time, tackles the themes of parents versus children and love versus hate, and the play continues to be read and produced widely around the world. But understanding Shakespeare’s so-called history plays can require a knowledge of several centuries of English history. Consequently, ______.
content.question_text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: many theatergoers and readers today are likely to find Shakespeare’s history plays less compelling than his tragedies.
choices.B: some of Shakespeare’s tragedies remain relevant to today’s audiences than twentieth-century plays.
choices.C: experts in English history are the intended audience for many of Shakespeare’s best-known works.
choices.D: experts in English history can best present Shakespeare’s history plays to any audience.

content.explanation: Choice A is the best answer. The passage details how the relevance of the history plays' themes may not be immediately apparent to modern readers, whereas the tragedies address broader, more timeless themes.

content.passage: The Mammillaria cactus M. boolii occurs naturally only in the state of Sonora in Mexico, and the smallness of its range makes it especially vulnerable to extinction. The traditional single-species approach to conservation emphasizes the need to focus on individual species most at risk, like M. boolii, but recently, conservationists have argued that an ecosystem-based approach that incorporates the many interactions between the climate, terrain, and various species of a given geographic area may be equally effective. This latter view is correct, the single-species approach to the conservation of M. boolii could thus ______.
content.question_text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: lead to a better understanding of how the distribution of Mammillaria species throughout Mexico has affected their survival.
choices.B: allow conservationists to better consider how climate changes affecting Sonora may reduce the number of species competing with M. boolii.
choices.C: erroneously shift the conservation efforts away from M. boolii itself.
choices.D: be more effective if combined with occasional surveys to ensure that the overall distribution of members of the species is increasing.

content.explanation: Choice D is correct because it suggests that integrating species surveys with the ecosystem-based approach could enhance efforts to maintain or increase the distribution of endangered species like M. boolii.

content.passage: In the early nineteenth century, some Euro-American farmers in the northeastern United States used agricultural techniques developed by the Haudenosaunee (Iroquois) people centuries earlier, but it seems that few of those farmers had actually seen Haudenosaunee farms firsthand. Barring the possibility of several farmers of the same era independently developing techniques that the Haudenosaunee people had already invented, these facts most strongly suggest that ______.
content.question_text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: those farmers learned the techniques from other people who were more directly influenced by Haudenosaunee practice.
choices.B: the crops typically cultivated by Euro-American farmers in the northeastern United States differed from those cultivated by the Haudenosaunee.
choices.C: traditional Haudenosaunee techniques were widely used in regions outside the northeastern United States.
choices.D: Euro-American farmers only began to recognize the benefits of Haudenosaunee farming techniques late in the nineteenth century.

content.explanation: Choice A is the correct answer because it most logically completes the text's assumptions of indirect transmission of farming techniques among European-Americans, despite their lack of direct contact with the original Haudenosaunee farms.

content.passage: The domesticated sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) descends from a wild plant native to South America. It also populates the Polynesian Islands, where evidence confirms that Native Hawaiians and other indigenous peoples were cultivating the plant centuries before seafaring first occurred between islands of ocean separating them from South America. To explain how the sweet potato was first introduced in Polynesia, botanist Pablo Muñoz-Rodríguez and colleagues analyzed the DNA of numerous varieties of the plant, concluding that Polynesian people visited South America over 10,000 years ago. Their findings indicated that whereas Polynesian people only used the plant to a limited extent, agricultural communities in that region ______.
content.question_text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: the cultivation of the sweet potato in Polynesia likely predates its cultivation in South America.
choices.B: the cultivation of the sweet potato from South America resulted in its introduction to Polynesia.
choices.C: created a number of new varieties before the plant reached Polynesia.
choices.D: were unlikely to have introduced the crop to growers in the islands.

content.explanation: Choice C is correct because it relates directly to the idea of varied cultivation in South America that could result in the transference to Polynesia, lending support to Polynesian introduction to the islands.
